criteria.criterion: athena.toml `[agents] env_pass_if_set` includes GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, and `env_pass` is unchanged. The comment above the list mentions GitHub.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. A new line `"GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_HOST", "GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN",` is added to env_pass_if_set. `env_pass = ["HOME", "PATH"]` is untouched. The comment now reads 'GitHub credentials for the steward's read-only `gh` (D96)'.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`. A new env.rs test shows that GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN appear in the built environment when the lookup supplies them, and are absent when unset or empty.
criteria.evidence: `env::tests::github_credentials_pass_only_when_set_and_not_empty ... ok`, and 35 passed, 1 ignored. The test's `agents()` helper parses the real athena.toml through `include_str!("../../../athena.toml")`, so the test would fail without the config change. It checks both values when set, and checks that both are absent when the lookup returns None or an empty string.

criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new decision, in the same format as D53, that explains why gh failed (an empty agent environment with no GitHub variable). It names the alternatives (a gh config under HOME; no access with a recorded blind spot) and the tradeoff of a token in the agent environment.
criteria.evidence: D96 uses D53's fields (Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance) and adds Case, as recent entries D94 and D95 do. Case gives the empty environment with no GitHub variable and cites env.rs and athena.toml. Alternatives (a) is a gh config under HOME and (b) is no access with the blind spot recorded. Tradeoff says the token reaches every agent role and recommends a read-only token.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md's GitHub bullet names the variables passed and tells the owner to export a read-only token. The steward docs state that without it the `github` blind spot is reported.
criteria.evidence: The bullet names GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_HOST and GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN with D96. It says 'The owner should export a read-only token before running Athena', warns against write scope, and ends 'Without a token the steward reports the `github` blind spot.' The steward brief in steward.rs now also names GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy`. Both pass, including any test that parses athena.toml.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings. `cargo test --locked -q` reported ok for every test binary with 0 failed; the env tests that parse athena.toml passed.

findings.summary: A line in D96 is longer than the wrap width the rest of the file uses.
findings.evidence: The line 'Follows D04 and D53 in using the allow-list. `env_pass_if_set` includes `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_HOST` and' is longer than the ~115-character lines around it.

findings.summary: Whether gh actually becomes readable depends on the owner exporting a token, and the change cannot show that.
findings.evidence: D96's Provenance says the owner's shell was not checked. The reading accepted this, and the docs tell the owner to export a read-only token. This is a limit of the snapshot, not a defect in the change.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the root cause: the GitHub variables were missing from the allow-list that builds every agent's environment, so `gh` never saw a token. athena.toml now passes GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_HOST and GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, each only when it is set and non-empty, and `env_pass` is unchanged. A new env.rs test reads the real athena.toml and checks that the two token variables pass when set and are dropped when unset or empty. I ran `cargo test -p athena-agent` (35 passed), the full `cargo test --locked` (0 failures) and clippy with `-D warnings` (clean). Decision D96 explains the cause, both alternatives and the tradeoff that the token reaches every agent role. roles-and-ladder.md, the steward brief, the README and the CHANGELOG all tell the owner to export a read-only token, and say that without one the `github` blind spot is still reported. Every changed file is on the deliverables list, and only variable names are committed, no token values. One limit: gh only becomes readable once the owner exports a token, which this snapshot cannot show. One nit: a line in D96 is longer than the file's usual wrap width.
